Figure 5:Before and after, on images it never saw: the repair found on text gives the damaged copy its answers
back.Image problems chosen by a rule fixed before any answer was read: in the order of the problems, the first of
MMStar, HallusionBench, POPE and ScreenSpot-v2 on which the damaged copy is wrong and the repaired copy is right. Upper
box: the end of the damaged copy’s answer and how it is graded (only the reply after the model’s last</think>counts, its boxed answer or else its stated answer); lower box: the end of the answer after the
model’s own repair, with the same seed; underneath, the base model’s result. Excerpts are verbatim, omissions marked by
an ellipsis. On ScreenSpot-v2 the box marks the target and the ring the click of the repaired copy.

Figure 28:The loop, as the 27B model found it in its own hidden states.Computed from the two hidden-state
reads the model requested in its first session: the last 100 positions read (a read stops at 8,192 tokens) of one of its looping answers and of one of its
answers that finished (with a wrong answer, as it happens). (a) Cosine similarity between hidden states a given number of tokens apart (centred over
positions), in three layers. While it loops, the model returns to almost exactly the same state every 32 tokens; in
the finished answer there is no such period. (b) Similarity between every pair of positions of the looping answer
in layer 32: the stripes are the loop.
